take_homes: Access is not use. Licences issued and people actually working differently are two numbers, and we only report the first.
Ask 'what would have to be true for them to switch?' about whatever they use today, before pushing any tool at a colleague.
The agent will happily write a polished technical plan and leave the people side vague. Check that side yourself.

monday.move: Pick one team lead and ask how they do a specific recurring job today. I am not showing them any tool. Then see whether the answer changes my plan.
monday.who: One team lead in business development, the one who ignored the last portal we rolled out
monday.stop_condition: If the conversation shows nothing about how they do the job that I didn't already know, I drop it. I will not build the agent.
monday.blocker: The calendar, full of the previous programme's steering groups. I will probably also not run the agent exercises myself.

misconception.why: The module did not show me anything to make me believe agents are different from agile. It was honest that adoption is a people problem and that its own project stalled, which is more than the last programmes managed. I still think wait and see is reasonable, but I am less sure it is the only safe move, and the tests are cheap enough to try.

one_line: The honest part is that tools do not get used just because you hand them out, and the author admits his own project stalled. The 'rapidly evolving landscape' filler paragraphs are exactly the slides I came to avoid.
